result.title: Breaking Information Islands in Sparse Tuning via Small-World Connectivity
result.summary: Sparse tuning is widely used to adapt large language models due to its parameter efficiency. However, its effectiveness depends not only on the number of trainable parameters, but also on the feature-interaction topology of the sparse update's structural support. Limited or uneven connectivity in this support may isolate subsets of feature dimensions, forming information islands that restrict direct task-specific interactions through the trainable update. To address this issue, we propose Small-World Induced Fine-Tuning (SWIFT), a sparse tuning framework inspired by small-world connectivity. SWIFT combines block-diagonal sparse updates for local feature mixing with a fixed deterministic scattering permutation that routes the mixed outputs across feature groups without additional trainable parameters. We further show theoretically that certain random sparse-update models and block-diagonal updates can exhibit information islands, whereas a sufficiently scattering permutation guarantees positive block-level expansion when the trainable block-diagonal factor consists of equal-sized, structurally dense square blocks. Extensive experiments on commonsense reasoning, natural language generation, and image classification demonstrate that SWIFT outperforms the evaluated parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) baselines on average and can match or surpass full fine-tuning. Implementation is available at https://github.com/xianchaoguan/SWIFT

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SWIFT 稀疏微调框架：用块对角稀疏更新实现局部特征混合，再加一个固定、无额外参数的散射置换把混合结果路由到其他特征组，并从理论上说明「信息孤岛」问题及该置换带来的块级扩张，在常识推理、文本生成和图像分类上平均优于多个 PEFT 基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「信息孤岛」诊断与固定置换打通特征子空间的做法，可能可供核查 latent 推理状态如何跨子空间混合、避免内部表示分裂为孤立分组；但论文不涉及视觉证据或推理期 latent 生成，只提供结构性方法线索。
